what_was_done: render_config no longer hand-types a second key list: it walks config.SPECS, lays the detected values over the SPECS defaults, and writes no delivery.protected_paths at all - the loader computes it from [release], so the AU-T2-15 fix is live on every init'd project (editing release.changelog moves protected_paths). New tests: the keys init writes are exactly SPECS's sections and keys (minus the protected_paths and hooks.rules composites), every undetected value equals its SPECS default, and editing release.changelog after init moves protected_paths.

Restart-proofed init: ensure_excludes runs before the mount and on the ready path (a run killed between mount and exclusions finishes on the next run); mount_state runs 'git worktree prune' and clears a .factory that holds only the worktree's own .git pointer, so a worktree add killed halfway neither wedges the next run nor needs the person to move anything. Tests: exclusion step killed (the second init writes what the first skipped), worktree add killed with the directory moved aside, interrupted pointer accepted, plus mount-level tests for the prune and the pointer cleanup.

_create_branch runs 'git update-ref refs/heads/factory-artifacts <commit> ""' (the empty old value decision 3 and the module docstring promise). When the update fails because another init created the branch, the loser re-reads the branch, checks it holds factory.toml, and takes the mount path with created=false instead of silently replacing the branch. Test: a first branch created by hand, then init, asserts ready, created false and an unchanged branch tip.

The non-empty .factory with no state in it is refused up front for both the none and unmounted conditions, before any branch is created; only an interrupted mount's bare .git pointer passes. A refusal can no longer leave a freshly created state branch behind, and the crash path through worktree add is gone. Test: planting junk under .factory for both conditions, asserting exit 2, the move-it-aside message and no factory-artifacts ref afterwards.

An unmounted legacy branch (STATE.md, no factory.toml on factory-artifacts) is reported, not mounted: init returns state legacy, mounted false and next holding 'vsdd import --dry-run' and 'vsdd import'. Test builds the legacy branch on the state branch name and asserts nothing is mounted and the import commands are in next.

A partial project now exits 1 with the init fields (state partial, mounted false) and next naming /vsdd-factory:status --fix, per plan 3.6, instead of exiting 2 with no fields. test_init_partial_refuses updated to pin exit 1, the state field and the next steps.

cli.main guards the dispatch.main call the way the import is guarded: SystemExit re-raised, everything else printed as 'vsdd: <type>: <text>' with exit 2. In dispatch.main the start directory is looked up lazily inside the try (an absolute -C works from a deleted working directory; a bare call from one exits 2 with a message instead of a traceback), and the --version branch sits inside the try, so an unreadable manifest is a caught Refuse exiting 2. cli.plugin_version deleted as dead code. Tests: deleted-working-directory runs, --version with a broken manifest, and the launcher test still passes.

json_requested is read from the raw tokens (after the -C strip) before _resolve, so an unknown command, a broken cmd_ module, a broken package or duplicate words all print one {"ok": false, ...} object on stdout under --json. Tests: the unknown-command and broken-module cases now assert the JSON line, and a new broken-package case asserts it too.

check_paths reports an error Problem with code 'unreadable' for a file in the artifact territory that cannot be read or decoded, instead of skipping it. cmd_validate refuses an explicit PATH that does not exist or is not a file. Tests: an invalid-UTF-8 story surfaces as an unreadable error and validate exits 1; a missing explicit path exits 2 naming the file.

changed_paths reads 'git status --porcelain=v1 -z -uall', splits on NUL (never C-quoted), consumes the paired original path of a rename, and prefixes '.factory/' without stripping - so '.gitkeep' is no longer mangled to '.factory/gitignore'-style names and spaces and non-ASCII letters come back whole. Test extends test_changed_paths with a dotfile, a name with a space and a non-ASCII name, asserting the exact paths.

check_text enforces the 1,000-character body-line limit as a size_cap, naming the line number and its length. New fixture invalid_long_line.md (a 5,047-character body line) and a case in test_each_reason_code asserting the line number is named.

ensure_excludes writes a newline first when the exclude file lacks its trailing newline, and the rewrite goes through a temporary file with os.replace. Test: an exclude file ending '# one\n*.log' comes out as *.log\n plus the two patterns, with no '*.log.factory/' gluing and no leftover temporary file.

test_raw_command_gets_tokens asserts the exact tokens list (['story', '--', '--json', 'why']); test_retry_command asserts the exact retry_command text ('vsdd again one two'); test_path_class_precedence adds a path matching both the tests and source globs (source widened to '**' via set_keys, precedence still picks tests); test_key_table_parity's vacuous second loop replaced with the real assertion that loading fills every SPECS key; test_import_loads_no_submodule now checks that one lookup adds exactly the owner module plus its intra-package import; the relayed-object cases validate against survey.schema.json with vsdd.schema and gained a ConfigError case.

Added the origin mount: a state branch pushed to a bare remote, cloned, and init asserts ready, created false, mounted true and the upstream tracking origin/factory-artifacts. test_init_resumes_after_interruption now really interrupts: mount_state patched to die after the branch exists (branch present, re-run mounts, created false), plus a separate test for the exclusion step dying. The local-mount repetition is gone.

The overclaiming outcomes in rewrite/findings/outcomes/step3-state-core.json are re-recorded: AU-S2-03 and AU-T2-13 as left-for-builder (the code settlement stands; the duplicated 'one key list' claims in tables/config-keys.toml and topics/project-configuration.md remain for the documentation pass; the config/hooks.md 'three rules' is corrected to four), AU-P2-03 and AU-S2-09 as left-for-builder (prelude_limits predates the unit and was only pinned by a test; the render_config restatement is gone after fixing S3R-state-core-1; the G2/S4/B6/H duplicates remain), AU-T2-15 finished properly (init writes no protected_paths copy; test_editing_release_changelog_moves_protected_paths), AU-S2-12 finished (commands/validate.md now states the one syntax and supersedes packaging.md's row), AU-P2-17 as left-for-builder (code half stands, the not-built command list was not copied into prose), and P3OPS-11's text corrected (the report-format keys were not added; they are P3COV-04's change).

A relative -C resolves against the cwd argument when main was given one, else against the process directory, via os.path.abspath - absolute and no symlink resolution. Invocation.start is always absolute and init reports an absolute root. Test: a relative -C of '../rel/proj' from a sibling directory succeeds and an absolute-start echo shows the caller's directory verbatim.
A leading --help or -h prints the commands() table with each Command.summary and exits 0. Test asserts the built-in commands and their summaries, and a stub package's command.

commands() and _load_command raise RegistrationError for a Command with empty words or whose first word does not match the module's family (derived from the cmd_<family> stem). Test: a cmd_stray.py registering ('elsewhere',) and a cmd_blank.py with words=() each raise RegistrationError naming the module.

The registry validates the decision-7 type grammar (scalars, ref:<kind>, list[...], allowed-value lists, untyped optional keys) at compile time and checks every ref: target resolves to a kind with an id row or a constant pattern after the table is compiled - both RegistryError naming the row, so a bad cell can no longer build cleanly and explode later inside check_text. Test patches the policy table with an unknown type, a dangling ref: target and a bad list-member type, each raising, and a good row compiling.

The un-initialised refusal names the detected condition ('...not an initialised vsdd-factory project (condition 'none'); run /vsdd-factory:setup'), and once a command is resolved the stderr label uses command.words, so positional arguments no longer appear as command words. Test asserts 'condition' in the message and 'vsdd lab:' (not 'vsdd lab positional:') for a usage error.

caps.waived now matches both forms: the project-relative path and the path relative to the state directory, which is the spec example's form. Test: a waiver written as 'stories/E-9/S-9.01.md' skips the cap, the .factory/-prefixed form still does, and a waiver for another file leaves the cap firing.

Any level-3 heading starting 'AC-' that is not in the '### AC-N (<contract>)' form is flagged criterion_contract, so spellings like '### AC-1: Title (BC-...)' escape neither the contract check nor the uniqueness check silently. Test: two malformed spellings, each producing a named problem.

detect_values derives branches.protected from the detected release branch (a project releasing from master protects master), and render_config writes it. test_init_detection asserts config branches.protected == [branches.release].

git() strips the repository-locating GIT_DIR, GIT_WORK_TREE, GIT_INDEX_FILE, GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY, GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES and GIT_COMMON_DIR variables from the inherited environment (a caller-provided env still wins), maps a missing git binary to GitError with returncode 127, and decodes the timeout's bytes-valued stderr. Tests: GIT_DIR/GIT_WORK_TREE set in the environment do not redirect a rev-parse from cwd; a missing binary raises GitError; the timeout message carries no b'' bytes spelling.

glob_regex translates '**/' to '(?:.*/)?' (consuming the slash), so '**/x' and 'a/**/b' match zero directories: a root-level tests.rs is inside the spec example's tests class. test_glob_semantics covers both shapes.

validate counts only files the artifact territories actually check (the whole-tree count went from 'everything under .factory' to the artifact files), refuses --changed together with explicit PATHs as a usage error, and uses the new public artifacts.tree_rels instead of the private _tree_rels (kept as a thin alias for the package's own callers). Tests: the whole-tree count is exactly the three artifact files, --changed with a path exits 2, and a missing path is refused.

_package_dirs skips a package only when importlib.util.find_spec returns None; a package that is there but fails to import raises Refuse naming the package and the import error, so its commands report the real fault instead of 'no command matches'. Test: a package whose __init__ raises ImportError gives exit 2 with 'failed to import', never 'no command matches', and prints the --json object.

test_init_through_bin_vsdd puts the directory of shutil.which('uv') on the PATH it passes instead of a hardcoded /opt/homebrew/bin, and test_import_error_exits_2 adds both the uv directory and the directory of sys.executable, running the launcher from the scratch copy so no working-directory .venv participates. Both pass regardless of where uv lives.

invalid_id_mismatch.md is used in test_each_reason_code (id_mismatch under the wrong file name); _planted_project takes tmp_path, ending the temporary-directory leak; test_config_command_prints_merged_data asserts the merged project name equals the project directory's name instead of an always-true tautology; test_path_command gained --json cases asserting the id, kind, path and exists fields on the hit and the two misses.

The 'ready' row of topics/state-directory.md now says the configuration file exists and the mount test passes, and that an invalid file is reported by the loader - matching the plan and the code (the mount test reads the worktree's HEAD, not the configuration).
